name: Process pool subscriptions, redemptions and switches
summary: The model manager's unit pricing team acts as transfer agent for its pools: it issues units when a client invests cash, cancels units when a client withdraws, and processes switches when a portfolio is rebalanced between pools. An analyst checks the instruction is authorised and before the cut-off, warns the pool managers of the flow, records it in the register with a second analyst's check, prices it at the unit value for the dealing date, arranges the cash or securities transfer with the cash team's dual authorisation, and confirms units to the client after the manager signs off. Pools have a few very large unitholders, so a single wrong price, date or account can move hundreds of millions of dollars between clients; most elapsed time is notice before the dealing date and the overnight wait for the price.

baseline.org_archetype: A provincial not-for-profit asset manager of about 240 staff running four to five unitised pools for five client portfolios, keeping the unitholder register in-house on a custodian module with controlled spreadsheets.
baseline.notes: Unit transactions come from client cash instructions (pension payroll and benefit flows, insurance fund set-asides), monthly rebalancing switches and occasional transitions. 2021 state.

trigger: A subscription, redemption or switch instruction for a client account and pool arrives from client service, total portfolio management or an onboarding transition.
end_state: Units are issued or cancelled in the register at the dealing date's approved price, cash or securities have settled, the manager has signed off and the client has a confirmation; or the instruction is withdrawn.

volume.seasonality: Peaks at month end (pension payroll funding, benefit payments and rebalancing switches) and at year end and during client transitions or pool launches.

evidence.note: Organisation file pool unit transactions driver (tier C there): each client cash instruction splits into two or three pool transactions plus monthly switches across five portfolios and four pools. Daily dealing in public market pools at a peer (BCI) supports dealing on any business day.

steps.name: Receive the subscription, redemption or switch instruction
steps.description: The unit transactions analyst picks up the instruction from the transfer agency mailbox: a client contribution or withdrawal turned into a pool order by client service, a rebalancing switch approved by total portfolio management, or a transition order during onboarding. The analyst logs it in the transaction log with the pool, client account, amount or units, dealing date and source.

error.defect_description: Pool or dealing date logged wrongly.

evidence.note: Author estimate of an in-house transfer agency desk; instructions arrive by email or workflow with a signed form.

steps.name: Verify authority and instruction details
steps.description: The analyst checks the signatures or approvals against the authorised signer list in the account set-up record, confirms that client service recorded a call-back to a known telephone number for client-originated instructions, and checks that the pool, account, currency and amount agree with the client's cash instruction or the rebalancing proposal.

error.defect_description: A forged or altered instruction is not detected.

control.basis: Account set-up and investment management agreement: instructions only from authorised signers, verified by outbound call-back to a known number (business email compromise controls)

next.condition: missing approval, wrong account or amount mismatch

evidence.note: Call-back verification to a known contact is described by the source; the 8% return rate and times are author estimates.

steps.name: Return the instruction for correction
steps.description: The analyst emails client service or the total portfolio manager with what is missing or inconsistent and holds the order until a corrected, properly authorised instruction comes back. A few orders are withdrawn instead.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Check the dealing cut-off, notice period and pool limits
steps.description: The analyst checks that the instruction arrived before the cut-off for the requested dealing date, that large redemptions meet the notice period in the pool's subscription terms, and that the flow stays within any purchase or redemption limit the CIO has set for the pool's liquidity.

error.defect_description: A late order is accepted for the earlier dealing date.

control.basis: Pool constating documents and subscription terms: dealing cut-off, notice periods and CIO purchase and redemption limits

next.condition: late, short notice or above a limit

evidence.note: Purchase and redemption limits set by the CIO at a peer pool manager and cut-off times as a unit pricing control are described; share of late orders is an author estimate.

steps.name: Agree a revised dealing date or a cut-off exception
steps.description: The manager of unit pricing decides with the total portfolio manager or client relationship manager whether the order moves to the next dealing date or is accepted as an exception, for example a benefit payment that cannot wait, and records the reason.

control.basis: Pool subscription terms: exceptions to cut-off or limits approved by the manager and recorded

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Send the pool cash flow notice
steps.description: The analyst emails the pool's portfolio managers, the trading desk and the cash team with the expected subscription or redemption, the dealing date and the settlement date so they can invest new cash or raise cash in time, and updates the pool cash flow forecast.

error.defect_description: Notice sent with the wrong amount or date.

evidence.note: Daily monitoring of pool cash and forecast flows at a peer is described; the notice step and times are author estimates.

steps.name: Enter the pending transaction in the unitholder register
steps.description: The analyst keys the pending subscription, redemption or switch into the register module (with a controlled spreadsheet for switches and in-kind items): client account, pool, dealing date, amount or units and settlement accounts.

error.defect_description: Amount, account or dealing date keyed wrongly.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Second analyst checks the register entry
steps.description: A second unit pricing analyst compares the pending register entry field by field with the authorised instruction and initials the transaction log. The analyst who keyed the entry cannot check it.

error.defect_description: A keying error is missed by the checker.

control.basis: Transfer agency procedure: maker-checker review of every register entry

evidence.note: Maker-checker is standard in transfer agency; rates are author estimates.

steps.name: Correct the register entry
steps.description: The preparing analyst opens the flagged entry, corrects the field the checker marked against the authorised instruction, notes the change in the transaction log and sends the entry back for checking.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Wait for the dealing date
steps.description: The order waits until its dealing date. Client cash instructions usually arrive one to several business days ahead; rebalancing switches are often dealt on the next business day.

evidence.note: Author estimate of notice lead times including weekends.

steps.name: Wait for the approved unit price for the dealing date
steps.description: The unit price for the dealing date is approved by the pricing team the next business morning, after the custodian's overnight NAV run. Orders are priced only at the unit value struck after the order was accepted.

evidence.note: Forward pricing at the next determined unit value and unit issues on the valuation date are described; timing follows the pricing workflow.

steps.name: Calculate units issued or cancelled
steps.description: The register calculates units as amount divided by the approved unit price (or value as units times price for unit-based redemptions); for a switch it prices the redemption leg in one pool and the subscription leg in the other. The analyst checks the price used, the rounding to the pool's decimal places and the value against the instruction.

error.defect_description: Wrong dealing date price or rounding applied.

control.basis: Pool terms: forward pricing at the unit price for the dealing date, never a price known before the order (principle of NI 81-102 adopted for the pools)

evidence.note: Unit value equals net assets divided by units outstanding; forward pricing; in-kind share is an author estimate tied to transitions and pool launches.

steps.name: Prepare the cash transfer instruction
steps.description: The analyst drafts the transfer in the custodian portal between the client's account and the pool's account for the settlement date, quoting the transaction reference, and attaches the priced transaction for the cash team.

error.defect_description: Wrong account or amount in the draft transfer.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Prepare the in-kind transfer list
steps.description: For an in-kind subscription or redemption the analyst builds the list of securities to move at dealing-date prices, agrees it with the portfolio manager and the transition plan, and sends free-of-payment transfer instructions to the custodian.

error.defect_description: A security quantity or account is wrong in the transfer list.

evidence.note: Author estimate; in-kind moves cluster around pool launches and client transitions.

steps.name: Custodian moves securities free of payment
steps.description: The custodian books the free-of-payment transfers between the client and pool custody accounts across markets and reports completion; foreign markets can take several days.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Cash analyst verifies and authorises the transfer
steps.description: A cash and collateral analyst checks the draft transfer against the priced transaction and the account set-up, then gives the first authorisation in the custodian portal. Transfers above the second-signature threshold go on to a second authoriser.

control.basis: Payment release policy: the preparer cannot authorise; dual authorisation in the custodian portal

evidence.note: Dual control on payments is standard; threshold share is an author estimate given transfers of tens to hundreds of millions of dollars.

steps.name: Second authoriser releases a large transfer
steps.description: The manager of cash, collateral and treasury operations reviews the large transfer and its support and gives the second release in the custodian portal.

control.basis: Payment release policy: second authoriser above the dollar threshold

evidence.note: Dual control on payment release is described among BEC controls; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Custodian settles the cash movement
steps.description: The custodian books the cash between the client and pool accounts on the settlement date, usually the business day after the price is approved.

control.basis: Custodian's CSAE 3416 / SOC 1 controls over authorised cash movements, relied on by the model manager and the pools' auditor

evidence.note: Settlement within a fixed number of business days of pricing is described for public funds; CSAE 3416 reports cover service organisation controls; internal transfers at one custodian are usually same or next day (author estimate).

steps.name: Confirm settlement and finalise units in the register
steps.description: The analyst checks the custodian cash or securities statement for the settlement, marks the units as issued or cancelled, and agrees the register's closing units for the pool with the units outstanding the custodian will use in the next NAV.

error.defect_description: Units finalised before cash actually arrived.

control.basis: Register units agreed to custodian units outstanding; tested by the pools' external auditor

evidence.note: Reconciliation of units and recording on a trade date basis are described; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Manager reviews and signs off the transaction
steps.description: The manager of unit pricing reviews the transaction log entry, price, units, settlement evidence and register update and signs off in the log, or returns it with a query.

control.basis: Transfer agency procedure: manager sign-off independent of preparer and checker

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Fix the error found at sign-off
steps.description: The analyst corrects the price, units or log entry the manager queried, reverses and rebooks in the register if needed, and resubmits for sign-off.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Send the unit transaction confirmation to the client
steps.description: The analyst produces the confirmation showing the pool, dealing date, unit price, units issued or redeemed, value and the client's resulting holding, and sends it to the client's authorised contacts with a copy to the client relationship manager.

error.defect_description: Confirmation shows the wrong value or goes to an outdated contact.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Update investment accounting and client reporting
steps.description: The analyst posts the final units and values to the shared register extract used by investment accounting, client reporting and performance, and confirms the final amount to the pool's portfolio managers and the cash team.

evidence.note: Author estimate; revision share follows the pricing workflow's post-release error rate.

steps.name: Reprocess the transaction at a corrected price
steps.description: When the pricing team corrects a dealing date's unit price, the analyst recalculates the units, reverses and rebooks the register entry, arranges any compensating transfer and sends a revised confirmation after manager sign-off.

control.basis: Pool NAV error correction policy: reprocess affected transactions when an error is material (thresholds of 0.3% to 0.5% of NAV in comparable regimes)

evidence.note: Correction of units issued at a wrong price is described; times are author estimates.

exceptions.name: Unauthorised or incomplete instruction
exceptions.description: Missing approval, wrong account or amount mismatch; returned and resubmitted, occasionally withdrawn.

exceptions.name: Late order or pool limit
exceptions.description: Received after cut-off, short of the notice period or above a CIO limit; manager moves the dealing date or approves an exception.

exceptions.name: Keying error caught by checker
exceptions.description: Second analyst finds a difference and the entry is corrected.

exceptions.name: In-kind transfer
exceptions.description: Securities move free of payment instead of cash, with a transfer list agreed with the portfolio manager.

exceptions.name: Transfer rejected by authoriser
exceptions.description: The cash analyst rejects the draft transfer for correction.

exceptions.name: Price revised after processing
exceptions.description: A corrected unit price forces reprocessing and a revised confirmation.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from receipt of the instruction to the client confirmation
benchmarks.population: In-house transfer agency for daily-dealt institutional pools with forward pricing and next-day settlement

evidence.note: Zero to four days of notice before the dealing date (median about two with weekends), the next-morning price, next-day settlement and sign-off; public mutual funds must settle within two to three business days of pricing (NI 81-102), used as a cross-check. No published benchmark for pension pools found.

benchmarks.unit: business days after the pricing date for payment of redemption proceeds (2014 consolidation; two business days from 2017)
benchmarks.population: Canadian public mutual funds under NI 81-102 (not binding on the model manager's pools)

evidence.note: Stated in the consolidation; the move to two days in 2017 is noted in the source description.

benchmarks.unit: share of instructions returned for missing authority or detail

evidence.note: Author estimate.

pain_points.description: The register is a custodian module topped up with spreadsheets for switches and in-kind items, so every transaction is keyed, checked by a second analyst and reconciled by hand.

evidence.note: Organisation file assumption on the register; author judgment.

pain_points.description: Instructions arrive by email with signatures and call-back evidence that must be checked manually; email instructions carry business email compromise risk on very large transfers.

evidence.note: BEC losses and call-back controls are described by the source.

pain_points.description: Processing cannot start until the next-morning unit price is approved, so any delay in pricing delays confirmations and the cash teams' funding.

evidence.note: Forward pricing requires the price struck after the order; impact is an author judgment.

pain_points.description: Three separate approvals (checker, cash authorisers and manager sign-off) each wait for someone to be free, adding hours to every transaction.

evidence.note: Author judgment.

sources.title: Public Equity Pooled Fund Financial Statements, December 2021
sources.supports: Units issued and redeemed at a unit value equal to net assets divided by units outstanding on each valuation date, recorded on a trade date basis; open-ended pools where each client's units issued or redeemed depend on changes to its asset allocation; purchase and redemption limits set by the CIO; pool cash and liquidity monitored daily.

sources.title: Pooled Funds (BCI web page)
sources.supports: Peer provincial public-sector manager: clients hold units of pooled funds held in trust; unit price is market value divided by units outstanding; public market pools open daily and private market pools typically annually; expenses recovered through the unit value; custodian for public assets; SOC 1 audit of the manager.

sources.title: National Instrument 81-102 Investment Funds (unofficial consolidation as of 22 September 2014)
sources.supports: Forward pricing: units issued and redeemed at the net asset value next determined after receipt of the order, and backward pricing not allowed; payment for purchases and redemption proceeds within a set number of business days of the pricing date (three in this consolidation, shortened to two in 2017).

sources.title: RG 94 Unit pricing: Guide to good practice
sources.publisher: Australian Securities and Investments Commission and Australian Prudential Regulation Authority
sources.supports: Monitoring controls in unit pricing such as movements outside agreed tolerances and tracking prices against benchmarks; data feeds with stale prices, zero amounts and out-of-tolerance moves; reconciliations in each pricing cycle; incident and error logs; compensation when an error is 0.3% (30 basis points) or more; price as often as units can be bought or sold; batching of applications on the day a price is struck.

sources.title: The Pervasive Threat of Business Email Compromise Fraud and How to Prevent It
sources.supports: BEC losses of about US$1.7 billion from 23,775 complaints in 2019 (FBI IC3); the payer should always verify banking instructions by an outbound call to a known contact, never relying on caller ID or details in the email.

sources.title: Reports on Controls at Service Organizations FAQs
sources.publisher: Chartered Professional Accountants of British Columbia
sources.supports: CSAE 3416 (SOC 1 equivalent) reports on controls at a service organization relevant to user entities' financial reporting; Type 1 covers design at a date and Type 2 covers operating effectiveness over a period; used by user entities and their auditors.

sources.title: CP130 Treatment, Correction and Redress of Errors in Investment Funds
sources.supports: Proposed quantitative materiality threshold for NAV errors of 0.50% of NAV for funds other than money market funds (0.10% for money market funds), qualitative factors, aggregation of small errors over several valuation points, and the steps of identification, correction and redress.

assumptions: The model manager has not published its transfer agency arrangements; the workflow follows the organisation file's assumption that the register is kept in-house on custodian records with controlled spreadsheets, with practices drawn from a peer provincial manager (BCI) and Canadian public fund rules applied by analogy.
The case runs from receipt of the instruction to the client confirmation; the notice period before the dealing date (mode one day) is the largest wait.

interfaces.triggered_by shares: about half the transactions come from client cash instructions and four in ten from rebalancing switches; onboarding transitions and pool launches are occasional; the price input releases a few delayed cases.
The manager of cash, collateral and treasury operations is added as second authoriser although the process map lists only three roles; the role exists in the organisation file.
Branch probabilities and times are author estimates (tier C); no published time study of pension pool transfer agency was found.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file (Job Bank Toronto wages deflated to 2021, plus variable pay, times 1.35).
